metadata.title: Open-source social-science Agent Skills library
metadata.description: Macro-scan, personal-anchor, metacognition-audit — social-science methods that run inside your own agent. One command to install; analysis runs in your agent, not on this site.

hero.subtitle: Openwisdom packs methods from psychology, sociology, history, political science, and economics into agent skills — macro-scan, personal-anchor, and metacognition-audit. Install them into the agent you already use. Analysis runs in your agent, not on this site.

diagram.ariaLabel: Coordinate-field diagram: three value axes — macro, anchor, metacognition — with a primary datum cross marking your position

install.promptCopied: Prompt copied — paste it into your agent
install.cliPrompt: Install the Openwisdom CLI for me (social-science agent skills package manager — installs skills only, never calls models). Terminal: npx openwisdom install. Pick agents interactively (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex); scripts: -y --providers=claude --scope=project. Verify with npx openwisdom search / list. If the user already sees structure but lacks ownership / agency levels / when to stop: npx openwisdom search --tag orientation-pipeline then npx openwisdom install --bundle=orientation-handoff -y --providers=claude.
install.mcpPrompt: Configure Openwisdom MCP for me (stdio package manager: search/list/get/install/update/detect — no model calls). claude mcp add --transport stdio openwisdom -- npx -y openwisdom-mcp; or Cursor/Grok: command=npx args=["-y","openwisdom-mcp"]. Then detect_providers and install. If the user says they see the pattern but not what they vs company vs state should own, or when to stop: openwisdom_search({tag:"orientation-pipeline"}) → get → install skills [responsibility-scope, responsibility-bridge, analysis-closure]; invoke skills in the agent session, never MCP run.
install.cliNote: Copy the prompt → paste into your agent. Handoff pack after recognition: --tag orientation-pipeline / --bundle=orientation-handoff.
install.mcpNote: Copy the prompt → paste into your agent. Handoff trio: scope → bridge → closure (tag orientation-pipeline).
install.copyFailed: Copy failed. Select and copy manually.

harness.label: Into the agent you already use
harness.subtitle: A compatibility inventory — not a marquee of logos.

scenarios.title: Three scenarios, three acts of orientation
scenarios.subtitle: Each scenario is a runnable analysis workflow: when to use it, step-by-step inquiry, output structure, bias checkpoints.

macroScan.name: Macro Scan
macroScan.tagline: Break a situation, an industry, or a system into structure: actors, incentives, constraints, and trajectories.
macroScan.when: When a complex situation demands seeing the whole board before judging.
steps: Bound the situation and time horizon
Ship a checkable structure and trajectory

personalAnchor.name: Personal Anchor
personalAnchor.tagline: Place your situation on historical and social coordinates: which curve you are on, which stratum you stand on.
personalAnchor.when: For long-horizon choices — career, city, direction — when you need to know where you stand.
steps: Name the choice and its constraints
Locate yourself in history and society
Mark room to move and path dependence

metacognition.name: Metacognition Audit
metacognition.tagline: A checkup for your thinking: expose biases, blind spots, and evidence gaps instead of polishing conclusions.
metacognition.when: After a conclusion forms and before it ships, when thought quality matters.
steps: Replay the reasoning chain and evidence

layers.title: Scenarios cite theory; theory supports scenarios
layers.description: Scenario skills cite discipline reference cards in their workflows — each card defines one theory or method, its boundaries, and common misuse. Knowledge is layered and composable, not one monolithic prompt.

model.title: Scenarios cite theory; one library, not two products
model.subtitle: Knowledge is layered and composable. Select a scenario to see one reference it pulls. Maintained skills, community PRs, and listed entries share one catalog.

macro.name: Macro Scan
macro.refBody: Past choices lock later room to move. Macro-scan uses this to explain institutional stickiness and trajectory inertia — not a blank slate called “now.”

anchor.name: Personal Anchor
anchor.refBody: Personal-anchor places “I” on a narratable historical layer and group position — coordinates, not pep talk.

meta.name: Metacognition Audit
meta.refBody: The audit names how you harvest only supporting evidence and requires closing counter-evidence gaps before you ship.

library.blurb: Recommended scenarios, discipline references, and listed entries share the Skills catalog and CLI/MCP. Contribute installable methods via GitHub PR.

disciplines.title: Six disciplines, the skeleton of the library
disciplines.subtitle: Each discipline ships references and listed skills that scenarios can cite — no empty taxonomy.
disciplines.edgeNote: Cite edges: macro-scan → political science, economics, sociology; personal-anchor → history, sociology; metacognition-audit → psychology. Philosophy supports critique and conceptual clarity.
